sections.heading: INTRODUCTION TO COVID-19
content: COVID-19 is an infectious disease caused by the novel coronavirus. Largely unknown before its outbreak in
Wuhan, China, in December 2019, COVID-19 moved from a regional crisis to a global pandemic in just a
few weeks. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared COVID-19 as a pandemic on March 11, 2020.
As the virus is spreading rapidly at a global level, countries globally are trying to prevent further contagion
by adopting measures such as social distancing, contact tracing, self-quarantining, surveillance,
communication, and testing. So far, China, South Korea, Japan, and Singapore have managed to flatten
the curve, while the US, Italy, Spain, Germany, France, and Iran have imposed drastic measures to slow
down the spread and control fatalities.
Government agencies have announced special financial aid packages to develop preventive and curative
drugs, the purchase of critical care medical devices, and the fast-track approval of diagnostic tests. Various
organizations across the globe, such as the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) and Wellcome
Trust, are also coming together to accelerate and strengthen the efforts to fight the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.heading: COVID-19 HEALTH ASSESSMENT
content: It is an unprecedented crisis creating an enormous strain on healthcare providers across the globe.
According to the WHO, within 67 days, the first 100,000 confirmed cases were reported worldwide. It took
the first 11 days to reach 200,000 confirmed cases. In the next four days, the number reached 300,000
confirmed cases, while in another 12 days, the count reached one million confirmed cases.
Source: WHO and ECDC
As of October 5, 2021, the virus has spread to more than 221 countries, with over 235,175,106 reported
cases and close to 4,806,841 deaths.

Disease progression patterns are similar in most countries; however, flattening of the curve and disease
containment largely depend on various measures taken by each country. China and South Korea, for
example, have managed to control the spread of the disease by implementing severe countermeasures,
such as restricting travel; imposing city-wide quarantines, curfews, and lockdowns; building specialty
hospitals; increasing medical aid; and ramping up testing. Most other countries are trying to emulate these
measures to contain the spread of the disease.

sections.heading: COVID-19 ECONOMIC ASSESSMENT
content: The COVID-19 outbreak has not only affected the healthcare sector but also impacted the global economy.
It has had a significant economic impact on various financial and industrial sectors, such as energy, oil and
gas, transportation and logistics, manufacturing, and aviation. It is predicted that the global economy will
go into recession due to the loss of trillions of dollars. With the increasing number of countries imposing
and extending lockdowns, economic activities are declining, which would impact the global economy.

content: Source: The Economist Intelligent Unit
With the combined effects of the pandemic and the slump in global oil prices, investments are expected to
contract sharply this year, especially in the energy sector. Export growth is also expected to reduce
drastically. A recovery is expected in the second half of the year, provided there is no emergence of another
pandemic wave, and countries manage to control the spread quickly and resume routine.
China has managed to contain the spread and is currently on track to resume routine. It is expected to
recover in the second half of the year. However, the Eurozone, one of the hardest-hit regions, is expected
to undergo a recession throughout 2021. Within the Eurozone, Germany, which is a manufacturing hub,
would recover at a much slower pace than the other countries. The US economy is also expected to see a
slump, with unemployment set to rise; recovery will be slow and only seen in the second half of the year.

sections.heading: COVID-19 ECONOMIC IMPACT—SCENARIO ASSESSMENT
content: Recovery from this crisis largely depends on various knowns and unknowns, which most countries will have
to deal with and respond to. The speed and strength of the economic recovery will depend on the health
and economic responses and the agility and speed of implementing various measures.
In the recent past, the global economy has become substantially more interconnected. The adverse
consequences of various steps related to containment are evident from global supply chain disruptions,
weaker demand for imported products and services, and the increase in the unemployment rate. Risk
aversion has increased in the financial market, with all-time-low interest rates and sharp declines in equity
and commodity prices. Consumer and business confidence have also reduced significantly.
This has magnified over time, and the spillover is seen in other countries as well. The latest forecasts by
multiple sources predict a four percent decrease in the global Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 2020 and
a slow recovery, making the recession caused by this pandemic worse than the 2009 global recession.
Based on these forecasts, the global economy is expected to recover by 2021; however, for some
countries, including the UK, Germany, India, and Italy, recovery is predicted to take longer.
In this fast-changing environment, the full impact of the pandemic on the global economy may not entirely
be known. MarketsandMarkets uses three scenario-based approaches (epidemiology, health response,
and economic response) to assess the economic impact and recovery period at the global level. Countries
and regions are expected to have different impacts and recovery periods.

restricting movement and business activities. The economic impact is mounting, and the top economies of
the world are expected to enter a global recession.
To provide a perspective on various scenarios, we assume the factors that would impact the economic
recovery from the global recession.
In a realistic scenario, we assume that possible health and economic responses would help economies
bounce back partially in 2021 Q4. In Q1, Q2, and Q3 of 2021, countries will ramp up testing capacities and
critical healthcare services and increase financial aid availability. This will help contain the spread of the
virus. The economic recession will last until 2022 Q2; a slow recovery will be seen from 2022 Q3. This is
expected to be a ‘U-shaped’ economic recovery, with a gradual improvement in the economy.

sections.heading: MARKET DEFINITION
content: According to SAS Institute, predictive analytics is the use of data, statistical algorithms, and machine
learning techniques to identify the likelihood of future outcomes based on historical data. The goal is to
analyze current data to make predictions about future events.
Predictive analytics is a statistical and data mining solution that consists of numerous algorithms and
methodologies. These algorithms and methodologies are used for both structured as well as unstructured
data to extract business insights. Predictive analytics offers flexible, scalable, and advanced solutions to
help users make better-informed business decisions. It helps industries understand customer perception
by providing a competitive market edge and the ability to rapidly orchestrate business decisions.

Traditional analytics platforms use static and stored data to analyze simple or complex patterns and react
to any business situation. These platforms take days to analyze and weeks to act on the stored data.
However, predictive analytics has the advanced analytics capability of extracting meaningful information
from the present and historical data sets. It assists companies in determining data patterns, predicting
future outcomes and trends, anticipating events, spotting anomalies, forecasting using what-if simulations,
and understanding customer behavior changes. Predictive models and analysis are used to estimate
future probabilities with acceptable levels of consistency. Predictive analytics technology is the core
enabler of big data, allowing businesses to use historical data and combine it with customer insights to
predict future events. Big data is an ever-increasing technology that assists businesses in optimizing
processes and minimizing operational costs. The combination of real-time data streams, AI, machine
learning (ML), and predictive analytics can deliver competitive business advantages. Traditional analytics
and BI systems use the deductive approach for analyzing data. This approach works well with structured
data. Predictive analytics, on the other hand, applies the inductive reasoning analysis approach, which
deals with large datasets derived from ML, robotics, sensors, and AI. It uses algorithms that carry out
complex calculations on large data sets and discover interrelationships and patterns between them.
The predictive analytics technology is finally witnessing large-scale adoption. The history of predictive
analytics dates back to the early 1900s. Around 1940, organizations first started using basic
computational models for neural networks and linear programming. In the 1960s, corporations and
research institutions started using non-linear programming tools, which has led to the commercialization of
analytics. Predictive modeling was then applied to credit risk decisions, marketing techniques, and travel
and logistics. By the 1990s, predictive analytics models were implemented by corporate organizations and
tech start-ups. Today, many forward-looking companies have started using predictive analytics across a
range of disparate data sets to achieve greater efficiency. The technology is operationalized by companies
for their business processes. Globally, the predictive analytics market is witnessing significant growth
because of the transformation from traditional BI techniques to advanced analytics techniques. Many
studies related to predictive analytics have revealed that organizations that strategically use predictive
analytics outperform other organizations that use traditional data analytics approaches. From predicting
market trends to gaining insights into customer needs, predictive analytics can help businesses tap the
power of their data to exploit new opportunities and gain an advantage over their competitors.
Predictive analytics uses mathematical, regression modeling, statistical, neural nets, ML, genetic
algorithms, text mining, decision trees, clustering, and data exploration techniques to extract insights from
historical and current data. ML, AI, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and advanced condition prediction
are the most crucial features of an effective predictive analytics solution. NLP is considered a cognitive
capability for IoT that helps users interact with systems and devices using simple, human language. It
evaluates structured and unstructured data, such as emails, chats, and social media interactions.
Predictive analytics estimates which type of involvement will be required, where, and when.
The key benefit of predictive analytics is that it enables organizations to identify untapped opportunities
and exposes the hidden risks associated with large data volumes. Predictive insights enable organizations
to make the right choices at the right time for shaping the course of their business. The major growth
drivers for the predictive analytics market include the increasing volume of data generated across
verticals, growing focus on market and competitive intelligence, and rising need for advanced analytics for
future predictions. The predictive analytics market also faces many challenges, including changing
regulations leading to the restructuring of the analytics model, ownership and privacy of collected data,
and the lack of appropriate analytical skills. Factors such as complex analytical workflows and the diversity
of data models are expected to limit market growth. The market has many new opportunities, such as the
demand for real-time streaming analytics and the high adoption rate in small and medium-sized

The spread of COVID-19 has been disrupting the world, businesses, and economies and has impacted the
way of living of the masses and approaches adopted by enterprises for their business management. The
ability of enterprises to sustain this pandemic has become new normal for them as they shift their focus
from growth opportunities and concentrate on implementing measures to mitigate the impact of COVID-19.
The upcoming analytics projects are kept on hold owing to the pandemic. Several companies are
competing with each other to gain a single project. Businesses have already started their efforts to return
to normal and are facing multiple challenges in terms of the impact of the pandemic on their customer
base and operations. Meeting customer expectations in terms of optimization of processes and increased
security concerns due to the presence of various connected networks, rise in connectivity issues, and
decline in industrial and manufacturing operations are the key challenges faced by businesses. New
practices such as work from home and social distancing are creating the requirement of the remote health
monitoring of infected patients, smart payment technologies, and the development of digital
infrastructures for large-scale technology deployments. With an increased focus on health, there has been
a rise in the demand for health-related wearable devices. For instance, in August 2020, Fitbit announced
~34% growth in its smartwatch sales in the second quarter of 2020.
Based on components, the predictive analytics market is segmented into solutions and services. The
solutions considered for the predictive analytics market include financial analytics, risk analytics,
marketing analytics, sales analytics, customer analytics, web and social media analytics, supply chain
analytics, network analytics, and others (HR analytics and legal analytics). The services segment includes
managed services and professional services. Professional services are further classified into consulting,
and deployment and integration. The risk analytics segment is expected to account for the largest market
share and contributed a share of 17.1% in the predictive analytics market. The customer analytics
segment is expected to witness the highest growth rate during the forecast period, growing at a Compound
Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 28.2% during the forecast period.
Among deployment modes, the cloud segment is expected to grow at a higher CAGR due to improved
scalability and operational efficiency. By organization size, the SMEs segment is expected to witness a
higher CAGR due to the increased adoption of cloud-based predictive analytics solutions and services.
On the basis of verticals, the market is segmented into BFSI, manufacturing, retail and eCommerce,
government and defense, healthcare and life sciences, energy and utilities, telecommunications and IT,
transportation and logistics, media and entertainment, travel and hospitality, and others (research and
education and real estate). The BFSI vertical is expected to dominate the market because of the prominent
use of financial analytics, risk analytics, and customer analytics solutions across BFSI operations.
On the basis of regions, the market is divided into North America, Europe, APAC, Latin America, and MEA.
North America is expected to dominate the market due to early technology adoption and the presence of a
large number of solution providers. The growing technology investments and improving penetration of the
retail and manufacturing vertical are expected to drive the market growth of APAC during the forecast

chain analysis, and future outlook related to the predictive analytics market. Globally, companies are
rapidly adopting predictive analytics solutions and services to gain a competitive edge in the market. The
key players in the predictive analytics market include IBM, SAS Institute, Microsoft, Google, SAP, AWS, and
Oracle. These companies are continuously innovating their products and services to overcome large and
complex data challenges by using statistical algorithms and ML techniques to forecast future outcomes
based on historical data.

sections.heading: MARKET DYNAMICS
content: Predictive analytics solutions are widely adopted in North America and Europe, whereas the adoption rate
is substantially increasing in APAC. The key factors driving the growth of this market include the need for
digitalizing enterprise business functions to cater to the evolving customer preferences, the growing
necessity to enhance operational efficiency in times of remote working, the rapid proliferation of mobile
devices and 5G technology, and increase in the penetration of IoT- based devices. On the other hand,
security and privacy concerns over confidential data hinder market growth. The demand for personalized
mobile apps and websites and the adoption of disruptive technologies such as AI, ML, and big data are
some of the major opportunities in the market. However, the market vendors face various challenges,
including the lack of skilled personnel and issues related to IT modernization, which do not allow the
market to grow rapidly to take advantage of the increasing demand for cloud services.

content: Big data has captured attention among businesses and consumers. It has not only become a major subject
in technology and media, but has also made its way into many compliances, internal audit, and fraud risk
management-related discussions. As an integral part of business operations in every industry, big data has
influenced the adoption of predictive analytics worldwide. By leveraging the opportunities and challenges
of big data predictive analytics, enterprises can optimize vital business processes, functions, and
objectives. Predictive analytics enables organizations to meet stakeholder demands, manage data
volumes, manage risks, improve process controls, and boost administrative performance by turning
information into intelligence. Advanced predictive analytics solutions play a vital role in enabling an
effective Intelligent Enterprise (IE) approach, which helps create a single view across the entire
organization through the combination of standard reporting and data visualization.
Advent of machine learning and artificial intelligence
Digitalization in the current day and age has exponentially transformed the landscape of predictive
analytics, thereby encouraging predictive analytics vendors and service providers to adopt digitized
systems for in-store activities. Organizations are increasingly focusing on the re-engineering of businesses
with the help of the immense power of the internet and digital technology. The adoption of digital
operations assists predictive analytics solution providers in finding newer ways to tackle the evolving
challenges. Due to the digital transformation of retail and eCommerce businesses, operating costs have
reduced and positively impacted the predictive analytics market growth. The advent of AI and ML has
enhanced organizations’ ability to gather information, analyze it, and make quick decisions with minimum
human intervention. Organizations are also adopting AI systems to speed up investment decisions. For
instance, Fukoku Mutual Life Insurance has adopted AI to calculate payouts. AI systems analyze and
suggest Governance, Risk Management, and Compliance (GRC)- related changes. Therefore, they help in
monitoring and collecting the appropriate quality of data to meet regulatory standards. The introduction
and implementation of ML and AI have helped providers in understanding customer perceptions by
analyzing the data gathered from multiple sources. Enterprises have shifted their focus to deliver a unified
customer experience across all channels and provide offers in real-time by analyzing customer buying
Cost benefits of cloud -based predictive analytics solutions
On-demand predictive analytics solutions reduce the cost of BI for organizations by reducing the upfront
cost and total ownership cost of the analytics system. Cloud-based predictive analytics solutions enable
business organizations to effectively utilize their financial resources as it compensates for the overall
Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) and Operating Expenditure (OPEX) required for purchasing storage servers and
other hardware equipment for the support and maintenance of analytics operations. As a result of these
features, BI and business analytics vendors and new start-ups are offering predictive analytics solutions in
cloud, thus driving market growth. Some technology initiatives such as Google’s MapReduce framework for
distributed computing on clusters of computers and the Apache Hadoop framework make it easy for
analytics vendors to develop large-scale analytics engines that optimally utilize cloud. These analytics
engines enable users to derive valuable business insights from structured as well as unstructured data.

predictive analytics within their organizations, while 20% of payers and
providers planned to start using predictive analytics in the next year.

Changing regional data regulations leading to a time -consuming
restructuring of predictive models
Predictive analytics delivers a decisive data interpretation and provides a larger picture to decision-makers
to boost overall business performance. The modification of predictive models permits integration with both
software and services, depending on the level and nature of the analysis. Professional services are
necessary for customizing existing analytics solutions, which cater to particular data sets. As the predictive
analytics concept is still in the nascent phase, the availability of skilled labor is also limited. This is another
important factor restraining market growth.
Moreover, the changing regulations are considered one of the major factors slowing down the adoption of
predictive analytics among organizations. For instance, data regulations may vary from region to region and
country to country. General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) enables the European Union (EU) to monitor
and ensure the safety of EU citizens.
Compared to conventional solutions, the initial costs and time incurred for deploying predictive analytics
solutions are higher, due to the involvement of BI and data analytics expertise. Though the deployment of
predictive analytics solutions would reduce operating costs in later stages, the time consumed for
managing and updating regulations is tedious. Therefore, the adoption of predictive analytics solutions is
expected to witness a slower pace in small enterprises.

sections.heading: Data security concerns
content: The backbone of predictive analytics solutions, data, remains a critically important aspect that most
organizations find difficult to manage. The inefficiency of managing exabytes and petabytes of data has
increased the chances of security breaches and data losses. In today’s competitive marketplace,
marketing teams require real-time and secure data to deliver an outstanding customer experience.
Organizations are gathering data through multiple touchpoints and measure them virtually. Such data is
used in support and communication and may include a variety of data types. These data types comprise
public information, big data, and small data collected from customers.
This data can include permissions, individual preferences, and updated contact information on products,
services, and communication platforms. Hence, vendors need to ensure high-level data security to
maintain customer trust. Recently, cybercriminals have gained access to widespread tools to obtain
anything from passwords to secret questions and token-generated passwords. In such situations,
marketing and IT teams need to work concurrently, providing each other with insights on when and how the
data is gathered, processed, and used in operations.
Such potent cyber-attacks continue to hinder the widespread adoption of predictive analytics across data-
intensive industrial sectors. However, this scenario is expected to gradually change throughout the forecast
period as the benefits of technology adoption continue to outweigh the risks associated and with overall
developments on the data security front.

Integration of data from data silos
Extracting value from data has become a key requirement for companies to successfully mitigate risks,
target valuable customers, and evaluate business performance. In addition, monetizing these data assets
requires the availability of a sufficient amount of data. However, data consolidation from distinct data
sources into meaningful information can incite various new challenges for organizations, especially
centralized business enterprises. Data exchange and data ecosystem deliver tools to analyze the collected
data at a centralized location and help extract and cross-check business-critical components. The
development of data exchanges and data ecosystems varies based on the assumptions made in the value
of the data for each customer segment. Many predictive analytics providers offer unified data aggregation
and data analytics platforms to help users successfully aggregate and analyze data from disparate data

sections.heading: sources.
content: Furthermore, data exchange is a major concern for industries, such as BFSI and healthcare, which deal
with people’s confidential data. As the need for data exchange increases, it needs to be balanced with risk
mitigation capabilities. With companies adopting predictive analytics software integrated with data security
capabilities, data exchange is not expected to be a major issue in the near future.
Ownership and privacy of collected data
The market competition is increasing every day due to the introduction and expansion of new technologies,
such as IoT, big data, and ML. These technologies have significantly contributed to the number of
endpoints collecting data, thereby resulting in an increase in dynamic data that keeps changing/updating
every second. For every organization that predicts customer behaviors by analyzing the collected sets of
data, maintaining data privacy is a huge security mandate. Concerns related to the data ownership and
privacy of collected data pose potential risks to the identity of individuals. Therefore, organizations are
bound to follow certain limitations in data collection types, quantities, and methods. These limitations are
likely to vary from nation to nation across the globe. Therefore, enterprises must stay abreast with the
changing rules and data-related regulations.
Today, in the technology era, the advent of the internet has brought cybercrimes into the picture. Hackers
target data storage for financial gains and other reasons. The breach of data impacts organizations’
identity and security. Some governments hold enterprises responsible for damages triggered by the loss of
confidential data. Therefore, enterprises ought to implement the latest security measures to ensure the
privacy of collected data. While outsourcing data analysis to a third-party BI vendor, organizations must
ensure that the BI vendor appropriately secures firms’ data.

the future. This evolution is marked by the development of analytical tools and the advantages associated
with them for all potential users.

sections.heading: THREAT OF NEW ENTRANTS
content: The threat of new entrants refers to the force of new potential competitors who can capture the market
share of the existing companies in any market. Currently, the threat from new entrants in the predictive
analytics market is high, as there is high to moderate R&D expenditure, and moderate to low initial
investment is required. Several global and domestic players have an established base in the market. These
market players have a global presence and offer various predictive analytics solutions for various
applications. Various companies enter this market by adopting strategies, such as acquisitions,
partnerships, new product releases, and integrating applications. The growing demand for predictive
analytics solutions in emerging applications enables start-ups to set up their presence in the market.
Hence, the threat of new entrants in the predictive analytics market is high.

sections.heading: THREAT OF SUBSTITUTES
content: The threat of substitutes refers to the possibility of alternative products replacing the existing ones in the
market. Switching to substitutes will not be much expensive, especially for bigger corporations who have
standardized their systems with specific predictive analytics solutions regardless of an update. Some of the
predictive analytics business applications available in the market include functionalities such as Artificial
Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Data Mining, and Statistical Modelling. These advanced
functionalities enable efficient prediction and analysis.  An increase in innovation would translate to an
increase in a better experience, which further would be worthy for the users. Loyal customers may approve
or be able to afford the new prices, which would, in turn, provide better features. Hence, the threat of
substitutes in the predictive analytics market is moderate.

sections.heading: BARGAINING POWER OF SUPPLIERS
content: The bargaining power of suppliers refers to the extent to which the solutions and services
suppliers/providers pressurize end users of predictive analytics solutions and services. The suppliers of
predictive analytics solutions and services can influence the prices of the solutions and services
subscription-based pricing form. There are many suppliers or low switching costs between rival suppliers,
enabling users of predictive analytics solutions and services to switch suppliers/providers at a low cost.  As
a result, the bargaining power of suppliers is low.

sections.heading: BARGAINING POWER OF BUYERS
content: The bargaining power of buyers refers to the pressure that buyers exert on manufacturers of the predictive
analytics market. The customer base for the predictive analytics market is expanding day by day due to the
presence of established players and upcoming start-ups in this market. Several unorganized vendors
provide predictive analytics solutions and services at a low rate as compared to other major players in the
market. This increases the bargaining power of buyers in the predictive analytics market. Therefore, the
bargaining power of buyers in this market is high.

sections.heading: INTENSITY OF COMPETITIVE RIVALRY
content: The competitive rivalry within the industry refers to the extent to which market players exert pressure on
each other. The presence of various well-established players has intensified the level of competitive rivalry
in the predictive analytics market. Some of these players are Microsoft, Google, Oracle, IBM, Salesforce,
HPE. These predictive analytics solution providers have a strong foothold in the local and global markets
due to their strong product and pricing portfolio, integration capabilities, and well-established strategic
alliances. Besides these, there are several manufacturers in the unorganized sector, which collectively hold
a prominent share in the market. Thus, the intensity of competitive rivalry in the market is high.

sections.heading: AI AND PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS
content: Big data is a major driver for organizations to enhance their sustainability in a competitive business world.
As more data is generated and stored, the need for more efficient, effective, and precise processes is
increased. Predictive analytics is among those processes. It is the process of using data mining, statistics,
and modeling to make predictions. The predictive analytics solution mines and analyzes historical data
patterns to predict future outcomes by extracting information from data sets to determine patterns and
trends. When predictive analytics is paired with computational power, it allows businesses to identify their
potential customers by using personalized data collected over time. AI algorithms are increasingly
integrating the ability to identify key emotions and produce insights that make prospecting more effective

amounts of data to help them improve their decision-making processes and outcomes. The predictive

sections.heading: ML AND PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS
content: Nowadays, companies have been increasingly using ML-based predictive analytics. Previously, ML and
predictive analytics seemed to be two different and unrelated concepts, but the demand for effective data
analytics has brought ML algorithms to combine with predictive analytics. Today, predictive analytics
extensively uses ML for data modeling due to its ability to accurately process vast amounts of data and
recognize patterns. Predictive analytics and ML go together as predictive models that typically include ML
algorithms. These models can be trained over time to respond to new data or values, delivering the results
for businesses. Predictive modeling largely overlaps with the field of ML. When ML and AI are coupled with
BI tools, such as Domo and Tableau, business executives can make sense of big data.

sections.heading: IOT AND PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS
content: Predictive analytics are changing the way manufacturers provide maintenance services and opening new
possibilities for revenue streams. In the era of digital transformation, equipment is becoming more
automated and complex; equipment owners are increasingly looking for more effective maintenance
services to manage and maintain their valuable assets. With predictive analytics, manufacturers can offer
customers superior maintenance services that increase uptime, improve product quality, and reduce costs.
Software AG provides predictive analytics technology for manufacturers in its IoT predictive maintenance
solution. It brings together IoT, streaming analytics, and process analytics into an integrated predictive
maintenance solution. This predictive analytics solution directly taps into the power of IoT and data from
sensors and actuators embedded inside equipment to be maintained.

sections.heading: 5G AND PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS
content: Due to high bandwidth, low latency, and the ability to support higher end-point densities, 5G would allow

coming days, the world will witness smarter AI, self-driving cars, and smart factories with data analytics and
5G. Therefore, it becomes imperative to focus on the connection between the two technologies. 5G is the
key to drive ML integration with data analysis. As organizations collect complex data, predictive analytics
can have an enormous impact on decision-making. Analytics in 5G would evolve to learn from context,
predict what will happen next, and prescribe the best response.

sections.heading: INTRODUCTION
content: Privacy and data protection are integral parts of data analytics, as they involve the transmission of large
chunks of data and personal databases. Numerous standards have been designed and developed
worldwide by various organizations to help enterprises manage their businesses systematically and
effectively. These standards are generally set by a recognized international body or industry groups to offer
a common view of frameworks, processes, and practices, which organizations can easily conform to.
Regions such as Europe and North America, where massive volumes of data are generated, have been
following the standards introduced by these regulatory bodies. Various companies are also acknowledging
the importance of complying with the safety-related data regulations, and as a consequence, are trying to
comply with rules and regulations.

sections.heading: SARBANES-OXLEY ACT OF 2002
content: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 was signed and brought into law by the US Congress in 2002 to protect
investors from fraudulent accounting activities by organizations. The act made it mandatory for
organizations to provide financial disclosures to prevent accounting fraud. Financial fraud scandals faced
by Enron Corporation, Tyco International plc, and WorldCom were the main reasons for the implementation
of this act. The act has also set compliance policies related to electronic records for IT departments. A few
sections from the act are mentioned below:

sections.heading: ◼
content: Section 302 states that the senior management must certify the accuracy of the financial

sections.heading: ◼
content: Section 404 states that all publicly traded companies must establish internal controls and
procedures for financial reporting.

sections.heading: ◼
content: Section 802 contains three rules that affect record keeping. The first deals with the distortion of
original records, the second defines the period for storing records, and the third rule sets
compliances for electronic records.

sections.heading: GENERAL DATA PROTECTION REGULATION
content: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) is a regulation by which the
European Parliament, the Council of the EU, and the European Commission ensure the safety of EU
citizens from privacy and data breaches in an ever-increasing, data-driven era. The GDPR extends the
scope of the EU data protection law to all foreign organizations that are processing the data of EU citizens.
It delivers the coordination of the data protection regulations throughout the EU, thereby making it easier
for non-European companies to comply with the regulations. However, if the regulations are not complied
with, the company may have to pay 4% of its worldwide turnover as a penalty.

sections.heading: BASEL
content: It is a city in Switzerland and is the headquarters of the Bank of International Settlement (BIS), which
nurtures cooperation among central banks with the shared objective of achieving financial stability and
common standards of banking regulations. BIS hosts the meetings of the senior officials of the central
banks of the member countries (currently 27 nations). Basel Guidelines refer to the comprehensive
administrative standards framed by a group of central banks called the Basel Committee on Banking
Supervision (BCBS). The set of agreements mainly emphasizes on the risks to banks and financial systems
and is called the Basel Accords. The purpose of the Basel Accords is to ensure that financial institutions
have enough capital on account to meet obligations and absorb unexpected losses. Currently, the Basel 3
guidelines are accepted by the committee members. These guidelines were introduced in December 2010.
The financial crisis of 2008 was the major reason for the introduction of these new norms.

sections.heading: PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS MODELS
content: Several distinct models and algorithms enable predictive analytical capabilities to be achieved, which can
be applied to many use cases. Getting the most out of a predictive analytics solution and harnessing data
to make informed decisions requires determining which predictive modeling techniques are ideal for the
firm. Consider a retailer whose goal is to reduce customer attrition. They may not benefit from the same
predictive analytics tools that a hospital uses to forecast the number of patients admitted to the
emergency room in the next ten days.

sections.heading: CLASSIFICATION MODEL
content: In some ways, the classification model is the most basic of the various types of predictive analytics models.
It categorizes data depending on what it has learned from historical data. Classification models are useful
for answering yes or no questions and offering broad analysis that aids in making decisions. The
categorization model's versatility—and the ease with which it can be retrained with new data—allows it to
be used in various industries.

sections.heading: CLUSTERING MODEL
content: Based on related features, the clustering model divides data into separate, tiered smart groupings. If an
eCommerce shoe firm wants to run customized marketing campaigns for its customers, it may sift through
hundreds of thousands of data to come up with a strategy that is unique to each customer. However, they
may easily divide clients into similar groups based on common features and design tactics for each group
on a broader scale utilizing the clustering methodology. Other applications of this predictive modeling
technique include categorizing loan applicants into "smart buckets" based on loan qualities, identifying
high-crime zones in a city, and benchmarking SaaS customer data into groups to uncover global use

sections.heading: FORECAST MODEL
content: The forecast model, one of the most extensively used predictive analytics models, deals with metric value
prediction, forecasting numeric value for new data based on prior data learnings. This model can be used
wherever there is historical numerical data. A SaaS company, for instance, can forecast how many clients it
will convert in a given week. Multiple input parameters are also considered by the forecast model.

sections.heading: TIME SERIES MODEL
content: The time series model comprises a series of data points with time as the input parameter. It develops a
numerical meter based on the previous year's data and utilizes that metric to forecast the future three to
six weeks' worth of data. The number of daily calls received in the previous three months, sales over the
previous 20 quarters or the number of patients that showed up at a specific hospital in the previous six
weeks are all instances of use cases for this model. It's a powerful approach to examine how a single
parameter evolves over time with a level of precision that goes beyond basic averages. It also considers
the seasons of the year and any events that may have an impact on the measure.

sections.heading: OUTLIERS MODEL
content: The outliers model focuses on data entries that are out of the ordinary in a dataset. It may spot unusual

sections.heading: INTRODUCTION
content: Predictive analytics derives insights from a wide range of internal repository databases, external data, and
data sources to identify future risks and provide strategic insights for decision-making. Predictive analytics
solutions and services provide a deeper and broader analysis of sudden damages and hard-to-predict
events of low frequency but high severity. These solutions can help organizations reduce their total cost of
risk and create more effective strategies. They enable organizations to proactively respond to changing
business-related conditions, improve operations, and enhance customer interactions driven by real-time
insights. IBM, Google, Alteryx, RapidMiner, SAP, SAS Institute, and Oracle are some of the leading vendors
in the predictive analytics market.
This chapter includes predictive analytics solutions and services. The solutions included in this section are
financial analytics, risk analytics, marketing analytics, sales analytics, customer analytics, web and social
media analytics, supply chain analytics, network analytics, and others (HR analytics and legal analytics).
The services provided in the predictive analytics market are professional services (deployment and
integration, support and maintenance, and consulting) and managed services.

sections.heading: COMPONENTS: COVID-19 IMPACT
content: Due to the rapid global spread of COVID-19, the adoption of big data analytics tools is on the rise. The use
of AL, ML, and natural language processing by researchers and developers has increased rapidly to track
and contain COVID-19. Researchers at the Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI) are using big data
solutions and analytics to effectively comprehend COVID-19 from different angles. Recently, the institute
announced that it would offer government entities, research organizations, and verticals access to
innovative AI tools, as well as experts in data and public health to help combat COVID-19. According to the
State of BI & Analytics Report, 2020 - Special COVID-19 Edition published by Sisense in April 2020, the
company surveyed 500 data professionals in the US, out of which 49% of respondents have reported an
increase in analytics use and new opportunities across all departments post-COVID-19. Due to COVID-19,
55% of businesses have started using data to improve efficiency, 47% to support customers, and 45% to
predict future outcomes. Several big organizations such as AWS and Google Cloud have offered
researchers free access to open datasets and analytics tools to help them develop COVID-19 solutions
faster. A team developed an AI tool at UTHealth. This has shown the need for stricter, immediate
interventions in the Greater Houston area. At Stanford University, researchers have launched a data-driven
model that predicts the possible outcomes of various intervention strategies.

sections.heading: Fraud detection
content: Fraud attempts have seen a drastic increase in recent times, thus making fraud detection more important
and applicable across all the major verticals. These verticals include BFSI, retail, healthcare,
manufacturing, government, and law enforcement agencies. Fraud detection through its real-time, near
real-time, and batch analysis of all user activities, assists companies in safeguarding customer and
enterprise information, assets, accounts, and transactions. For fraud detection, predictive analytics uses
background server-based processes to examine users’ current behavior patterns and compares them with
their past buying patterns. Data mining technologies such as decision trees, ML, AI, cluster analysis, and
neural networks generate a predictive model to understand fraudulent activities across networks.

observed that many companies fall prey to heavy penalties because of non-compliance or due to the

governance, risk, and compliance management applications may cost a substantial amount of time and
money in the initial phase, but they provide a great value proposition for organizations and their clients in
the long run. It is necessary that governance and compliance work together and are aligned toward a
common set of goals and objectives, which organizations plan to achieve. Governance policies provide a

risk management performs the task of safeguarding enterprises from internal and external threats and
creates a value proposition for stakeholders. The compliance part provides a certain set of rules and
regulations that need to be followed to protect public and organization interests.

sections.heading: RISK ANALYTICS
content: Risk analytics mainly covers enterprise risks, such as financial risk and operational risks. It also covers the
risks associated with an organization’s network efficiency. Organizations use the risk analytics solution to
enhance their risk intelligence capabilities to fight risk exposures. By using advanced analytical
frameworks, companies can avoid, address, or quickly recover from major risk events. The risk analytics
technique measures, quantifies, and predicts risks from past data. It provides organizations with valuable
insights to make effective decisions and increase revenue while reducing risk costs. The risk analytics
process includes identifying risks, categorizing them according to priorities, and quantifying them based on
historical data, information from firms, and third-party establishments. Organizations are prone to various
types of risks, such as credit risk, hedging risk, governance risk, fraud risk, and technology risk, which can
be detrimental to their businesses in terms of loss of revenue and goodwill in the market. The risk analytics
solution in predictive analytics facilitates enterprises to establish a baseline for measuring risks across
verticals, such as banking and financial services, insurance, healthcare and life sciences, and retail and
eCommerce, by incorporating all the facets of risks together into a single unified system that provides key
decision-makers with adequate clarity in identifying, viewing, understanding, and managing risks.

sections.heading: Cyber risk management
content: Risk analytics enables organizations to mitigate cyber risks. Globally, losses arising from fraudulent cases
due to the lack of cybersecurity are increasing at a phenomenal rate, making it very important for
companies to properly plan cyber risk management in line with their business operational goals. Risk
analytics services for cyber risk prevention are evolving from financial loss, disruption, or damage to the
reputation of organizations due to the failure of IT systems. The government, BFSI, and healthcare verticals
are the key adopters of risk analytics tools in the cyber risk space. Cyber risk analytics helps government
organizations detect frauds and optimize investigators’ efficiency. The implementation of risk modeling
techniques into analytics enables them to identify probable frauds, the severity of frauds, and priorities for
investigations based on the impact rate of each fraud. Nowadays, consumers expect a safe and
transparent online shopping experience; thus, risk analytics solutions provide an edge by transparently
assessing the fraudulent risk of a transaction in real-time during authentication.

sections.heading: Operational risk management
content: Operational risk management assists companies in improving their risk processes, controlling and
optimizing capital allocation, meeting regulatory requirements, and mitigating the frequency and severity of
risk events. Companies in verticals such as manufacturing, transportation and logistics, and energy and
utilities are focusing on operational efficiency by using innovative technologies to avoid operational risks.
These verticals are taking initiatives for improving their core functions, such as demand planning, revenue
and workforce management, transit and pricing analysis, and the optimization of marketing and risk
management functions. Companies are implementing fraud and risk analytics for analyzing all potential
risks, such as operational, financial, as well as traveling. Risk analytics predicts the probability of
equipment and vehicle failure, accidents, and corporate and financial frauds through the analysis of
historical and present data.
Credit and market risk management
Credit and market risk management applications offer simulation-based risk measures at the required
depth for middle office risk analysis. These applications can help organizations proactively manage
regulatory credit risks using a single, end-to-end risk management environment. A transparent framework
and integrated data aggregation, analytics, and reporting capabilities provide enterprises with open,
flexible, and extensible means to measure and manage credit risks in a constantly changing regulatory
environment. Better credit and market risk management also present an opportunity to improve the overall
performance and secure a competitive advantage. Credit and market risk analytics helps companies retain
their customers, control fees, and decrease delinquencies.
Other risk analytics applications
Organizations are often surrounded by risks that might affect their numerous factors, in addition to the
primary operational area; these risks comprise reputational risk, environmental risk, third-party risk, and
economic risk. Environmental risks are concerned with manufacturing plants and chemical factories,
where chemical risk assessment is carried out to ensure that human health and the environment are least
affected. The third-party risk management approach consists of understanding the level and type of risk

sections.heading: Predictive modeling
content: Predictive modeling is a marketing technique that uses existing and historical customer data to analyze
and predict future behaviors. It helps marketers target the right customers and understand what products
or services they are looking for in markets. Predictive modeling allows marketers to use this knowledge to
wisely manage their marketing expenditure. It is a form of data-mining technology that works by analyzing
historical and current data and generating a model to predict future outcomes.

sections.heading: Yield management
content: Yield management is the marketing pricing strategy used by companies to increase their revenue based on
understanding, anticipating, and influencing consumer behaviors with limited resources. The objective of
yield management is to align timing, pricing, and customer buying patterns to achieve higher sales and
ROI. It helps control inventory to sell it to the right customers at the right time for the right price based on
the buying patterns of customers.
Product and service development strategies
It is essential to analyze the market data for both launching new products or services and refining existing
products or services to satisfy customers. Marketing analytics can help understand customer preferences
and needs worldwide; analyze the data from various channels, including social media, emails, and mobile
devices; and help marketers understand regions and products or services. They also help them develop
product development strategies based on demands and customer preferences.

Other applications of marketing analytics consist of demand forecasting and contact optimization. Demand

interconnected and help in optimizing customer contacts across the enterprise and getting the right offer,
to the right customer, at the right time through the right channel and distributors.

sections.heading: SALES ANALYTICS

provides fact-based comprehensive analytical insights on data. It helps sales executives to identify cross-
sell and up-sell opportunities for their existing clientele, analyze pipeline opportunities, generate business
from new clientele, maximize value from their Customer Relationship Management (CRM) applications,
and analyze customer spending trends. Sales analytics includes the features of predictive analytics
patterns to leverage varying customer behaviors and determine actionable sales targets. This solution
provides methods to identify, comprehend, model, track, and augment an organization’s sales
performance through predictive models. It is incorporated with BI tools that provide rich virtualization of
data in a graphical view. Sales analytics also helps sales representatives track customer and product
performance at every stage. It also assists them in generating leads and closing deals.

content: OCTOBER 2021 © MarketsandMarkets™
Sales life cycle management
A sales life cycle starts with product awareness through lead generation and ends with sales. Each step in
the sales life cycle involves various stages that are useful to understand where exactly the prospects or
leads are in sales pipelines. The sales analytics solution helps organizations efficiently manage the sales
life cycle and drive new business. It also helps provide insights into new leads, conversion history, and the
average value per marketing-qualified and sales-qualified lead. The results from the solution help make the
sales life cycle more efficient and generate more revenue. Sales life cycle management assists companies
in predicting new future revenue opportunities and changing consumer trends.
Sales rep efficiency management
Sales rep efficiency management assists companies in overcoming sales reps’ major concerns over
misrepresenting hundreds of opportunities. As a result, they often end up investing too much time in low-
quality opportunities and lesser time in valuable opportunities. The sales analytics solution helps monitor
the nature of these leads and prioritize them. Sales managers can optimize the efficiency of their sales
team by investing less time in pursuing lower-value opportunities.
Other sales analytics applications
Other applications of sales analytics include territory management and incentive compensation
management. The incentive compensation management application is designed to provide organizations
with a comprehensive suite of tools to manage, create, and distribute incentive data, compensation plans,
sales reports, calculations, and dashboards. This application lets organizations have accurate
compensation calculations, generate transaction registers, forecast incentives, and reduce errors of data
inaccuracies in spreadsheets. The territory management application provides organizations with a
channelized pattern to align their diversified sales teams. The alignment of sales personnel in territory
management is made across regions, product lines, and customer groups. This application
comprehensively helps organizations seamlessly align their customers under different territories to assist
sales teams in handling client requirements and queries.

sections.heading: CUSTOMER ANALYTICS
content: Customer analytics is an advanced and systematic analytical process, also known as customer
intelligence, in which customer data is used by companies to better understand customer behaviors and
make strategic business decisions through customer segmentation and predictive analytics. It is a
systematic analysis of customer insights, which assist organizations in identifying and targeting customers
for marketing programs from their behavioral prediction. It helps organizations retain the existing
customers, maximize the customer life cycle value, and gain customer loyalty. Data optimization is done by
combining processes and technologies, such as behavioral analysis, sentiment analysis over social media,
predictive modeling, segmentation, and data visualization and reporting. The analysis of voluminous data
offers a competitive advantage to organizations.

Customer segmentation and clustering
Organizations often have a very large amount of customer data, which may be different. Hence, they want
to segment it into different clusters. They often want to separately analyze each segment as customers
may have different preferences and different behavioral patterns. In such situations, customer analytics
can be used to identify similarities or differences between those observations. Customer analytics can also
be used to identify consumer segments or competitive sets of products. It is often necessary to split
customer data into segments and perform any subsequent analysis within each segment to develop
segment-specific insights. Clustering and segmentation techniques are used to group data observations in
a few segments so that data within any segment is similar, while data across segments is different. Cluster
analysis often requires a lot of contextual knowledge and creativity, which statistical tools can provide.

sections.heading: Customer behavior analysis
content: In predictive analytics, customer behavior analysis is the study of individuals, groups, or organizations and
the processes companies select, secure, use, and dispose of products, services, experiences, or ideas to
satisfy customer needs and wants. Most of the business decisions are based on purchasing behaviors and
customer preferences. These business decisions rely on the assumptions, knowledge, and analysis of
customer behaviors. Understanding and analyzing customer behaviors are essential for managers these
days. It helps them provide value to customers, create competitive advantages, and apply marketing
strategies based on purchasing behaviors.
Monitoring customer loyalty and satisfaction
Monitoring customer loyalty and satisfaction application are very important for organizations these days.
Customers may deal with companies/products through various channels, including in-store, website,
mobile app, promotional offer, Interactive Voice Response (IVR), and contact centers. The application is
essential to improve customer experiences while decreasing service costs. Companies can deliver
consistent customer experiences across channels. Every interaction, happening over any communication
channel, is an opportunity for businesses to improve productivity and gain customer loyalty. Customer
loyalty is increased by predicting and preventing customer churn.
Other customer analytics application s
Other applications in customer analytics consist of operational efficiency management and campaign
performance management. In predictive analytics, customer analytics applications help users with
operational efficiency by providing both data analysis and line‐of‐business users with self-service analytics
so that they can deliver deeper insights in hours. Customer analytics applications enhance operational
efficiency by delivering products or services to customers in the most cost-effective manner possible by
ensuring high-quality products, services, and support.

sections.heading: WEB AND SOCIAL MEDIA ANALYTICS
content: The web and social media analytics solution analyzes entire web and social media data. This analyzed data
helps in measuring, collecting, analyzing, and reporting the internet data for understanding and optimizing
web usage. This solution assists in monitoring traction and engagement with online customer messages,
while it also assists in exploring challenges and potential controversies around aligning marketing
strategies. The web and social media are becoming a source of valuable data in the form of customer
feedback through comments and prospects’ views on companies, their products and services, market
trends, and breaking news. Nowadays, large enterprises, as well as SMBs, rely largely on the digital data
gathered through their web portals and various social media channels, including Facebook, LinkedIn, and
Twitter. This is due to the rising need of digital marketers, advertisers, and publishers to segment their
premium buyers from other customers, track the overall visitor traffic on the website and social media
pages, manage ad campaigns, and improve complete web and social media performance. Web and social
media analytics caters to all these requirements and helps enterprises reform their business strategies
and add to online sales.

sections.heading: Social media management
content: Social media channels facilitate consumers with opportunities to proactively connect with others and
enable brands to engage with consumers in a two-way relationship. This interaction and communication
over social media platforms generate large amounts of data that can be analyzed to gain actionable
intelligence about content and campaign performance. Organizations can gain a competitive advantage by
employing web and social media analytics solutions to discover, sort, sift through, and analyze the
mountains of data present in these social media platforms. This helps them obtain capabilities to
recognize patterns in customer sentiment and measure their marketing and branding efficiencies.

sections.heading: Search engine optimization
content: Appropriate site architectures are critical considerations when it comes to the online marketing of websites
to attract potential visitors. In general, by tracking and ranking, any website can be advanced and modified
to generate high-quality services to improve its rank among the competitors in the market. Search engine
optimization has proved to be an effective and efficient tool in the predictive analytics market as it saves
time and effort by providing the exact ranking of each keyword input in multiple search engines. By tracking
the rank of each keyword and website traffic over any period, it becomes an easy task to modify websites.
Search engine optimization points to website areas that need improvement to get a satisfactory ranking
report to increase rankings.

content: Performance monitoring is one of the major applications of the web and social media analytics solution in
the predictive analytics market. It lets companies record servers' performance and identify anomalies,

waiting for a long time to download or play demo videos on websites. If servers do not perform well, a

sections.heading: Competitor benchmarking
content: Competitor benchmarking can be defined as the process of comparing firms’ practices and performance
measures with their most successful competitors. Benchmarking is a useful process to optimize
organizations’ strategies on social media and build new strategies inspired by competition. Analyzing other
brands having similar products and target groups helps to know the standing of companies and their
brands and what needs to be developed and improved. The purpose of competitor benchmarking is to gain
a level of insights and create a marketing strategy based on competitor insights. Through social media
benchmarking analysis, companies can know the best practices of social media and elements that provoke
weaker interactions on networks.

sections.heading: SUPPLY CHAIN ANALYTICS
content: Supply chain analytics consists of the complete value chain, sourcing, manufacturing, distribution, and
logistics. It aims at improving operational efficiency and effectiveness by enabling data-driven decisions at
strategic, operational, and tactical levels. It assists companies in delivering revenue growth, improving
margins, managing working capital in a better way, and enhancing overall control points across the supply
chain. Nowadays, companies across verticals witness petabytes of data generation in terms of volume
through data sources, such as ERP, CRM, Content Management System (CMS), Warehouse Management
System (WMS), and Transportation Management System (TMS), across the entire supply chain, from the
procurement and sourcing of raw materials to the manufacturing, distribution, and logistics of refined
goods. Thus, businesses need to extract useful insights from this huge data that helps business owners
make effective strategic decisions.

Distribution and logistics optimization
Supply chain analytics is used by freight forwarders, shippers, and Third-Party Logistics (TPL) providers. The
distribution and logistics optimization application assist shippers and TPLs in collecting and analyzing
customers’ supply chain data. The analysis of this customer-centric data is done with the help of high-end
transportation and logistics analytics solutions to unravel numerous valuable insights for shippers and
TPLs. These solutions ultimately help them reduce freight costs, which are measured on a ‘per mile’ basis.
They also help shippers and TPLs utilize their assets fully across the entire logistics value chain, from
carrier sourcing to load planning and management.

sections.heading: Inventory management
content: The supply chain analytics solution helps organizations optimize their inventory by effectively positioning
raw materials, work-in-progress, and finished goods inventory throughout supply chain networks. It helps
companies forecast demand better, reduce inventory levels with a minimal effect on sales or profits, and
better sync production with the distribution. The analysis of data collected using various sources, including
enterprise applications and sensors, uses an approach to ensure a lower total cost. The analysis considers
working capital investment, service performance, and operational costs, including variable handling costs,
inventory carrying costs, transportation costs, and backorder, stock-out, and lost-sales penalties.

sections.heading: Manufacturing analysis
content: The amount of data generated in the production department of businesses in verticals such as healthcare
and life sciences, and manufacturing is massive. Change is the new constant as far as the manufacturing
data is concerned. This is due to continuously changing market dynamics. The supply chain analytics
solution helps numerous business organizations working in and across different verticals to collect and
analyze the changing manufacturing data in real-time. This solution assists business executives in
analyzing comprehensive production processes, measuring the performance of the production processes,
and maintaining and enhancing the quality standards of produced commodities. It cumulatively helps
business organizations in reducing their overall production costs and increasing production efficiencies.
Other supply chain analytics application s
Other applications considered in the supply chain analytics solution are vendor performance management
and spend analysis. Predictive analytics provides companies with the risk model-based vendor
performance management and analysis application, which is based on external data and ongoing vendor
performance for efficiently evaluating and monitoring vendor performance to mitigate the future risk of
vendor failure. It offers users spend analysis to identify anomalies in their direct and indirect spend
through machine data analytics. This application uses analytical models on spend data to find anomalies
that indicate potential savings, such as contract non-compliance, rate mismatches, duplicate invoices, and

sections.heading: NETWORK ANALYTICS
content: The network analytics solution assists companies in identifying and resolving most of the IT infrastructure
issues before they impact operational performance, which might include memory usage, CPU usage,
routing events, Syslog analytics, pocket loss, performance thresholds, and latency variations. It helps
organizations monitor and analyze data running across networks. This analysis is then used strategically
for optimizing network performance and assists in taking proactive measures before any network mishap
takes place. The number of connected devices across the world would grow enormously in the coming
years with the increasing adoption of IoT, which, in turn, would be responsible for increasing the
complexities of networks. To tackle this situation and make a mark in the dynamic telecom environment,
the adoption of network analytic solutions is expected to rise significantly in the coming years.

sections.heading: Intelligent network optimization
content: An intelligent network provides specific technical capabilities or services outside the conventional network
standard spectrum. This term is often linked with telecom networks, as recent innovations have expanded
telecom capabilities beyond its original primary function of facilitating phone calls. The network analytics
solution helps organizations optimize the intelligent network.

sections.heading: Traffic management
content: With the increasing adoption of network bandwidth for multiple modes of communication, it is necessary
for telecom companies to manage network traffic to avoid network congestion. Customers always expect to
receive seamless network signals for continuous connectivity. The network analytics solution helps these
companies to manage network traffic by analyzing network data in real-time.
Other Network Analytics Application s
Other network analytics applications consist of managed network security and configuration change
management. Managed network security is segregated into identity and access management, Intrusion
Detection Systems (IDS)/Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS), antivirus/bot/malware, and other threats. It
refers to taking preventive measures for protecting network infrastructures from unauthorized access,
intrusions, or the misuse of networking components. It protects from several threats, including Distributed
Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) hopping, Domain Name System (DNS)
spoofing, and Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) spoofing. Network configuration change management is
the process of identifying and documenting network device configurations. The implementation of network
configuration change management reduces network downtime, optimizes network security, and automates
network changes, thereby minimizing configuration errors.

geographies. HR analytics enables organizations to align HR metrics with strategic business goals. Legal

content: The deployment modes in the predictive analytics market include on-premises and cloud. Predictive
analytics solutions are deployed in various enterprises. Enterprises adopt cloud models due to inadequate
resources. These models enable organizations to leverage the benefits of real-time predictive analytics.
Despite high latency, cloud deployment models are preferred by verticals to maintain and predict future
outcomes. The cloud segment is projected to grow in the near future.

sections.heading: DEPLOYMENT MODES: COVID-19 IMPACT
content: The COVID-19 pandemic has thrown everything into disarray on a massive scale. The epidemic, on the
other hand, has turned out to be a boon for the cloud computing industry. Cloud platforms can assist in
quickly launch new digital customer experiences and provide analytics at a lower cost than traditional
technology platforms. When governments worldwide instituted a lockdown to contain the virus in early
2020, businesses were forced to relocate to a remote working environment from their traditional brick-and-
mortar setup to maintain business continuity. As a result of this quick transformation, cloud-based
solutions are in high demand. Today, cloud-based analytics platforms are used by 47% of businesses,
according to an industry expert. COVID-19 has influenced the move to hybrid cloud systems, not just
because customers demand it but also because the previous solutions (totally cloud-based or entirely on-
premises) were failing. The COVID-19 outbreak is forcing numerous companies to review their IT strategies
as a top priority. Several organizations emphasize the importance of having the right cloud-based
collaboration tools, enabling employees to work remotely to limit the pandemic impact on productivity.

content: BFSIs are using real-time analysis to predict which customer segments are most inclined to acquire a

Additionally, banking and financial services organizations have to face frauds at different levels, which vary

content: The increasing digitalization and the growing use of connected devices have transformed the way the retail
industry is operating. Predictive analytics can help the retail and eCommerce vertical increase its
profitability by offering actionable insights related to changing customer behavior and patterns. Challenges
associated with increased globalization, the complexity of supply chains, and the growing competitive
environment have also fueled the demand for predictive analytics solutions. The growing complexity of
regulatory and compliance requirements, such as the Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act (CPSIA)
and Fair Packaging and Labeling Act (FPLA), is another driver for the adoption of predictive analytics
solutions by the retail and eCommerce vertical. Hence, the sector can integrate predictive analytics
solutions into its operations to cut costs, track regulatory requirements, and enhance profit margins. As the
industry is turning towards a more digitized approach, retailers are implementing advanced analytics
practices for addressing the major business challenges and maximizing benefits. Predictive models enable
businesses to determine the intent of their customers. These models assist retailers in meeting market
demands. Predictive analytics monitors historical product pricing, customer interests, competitor pricing,
and inventory to deliver the best possible prices to gain maximum profits. For instance, in Amazon’s
marketplace, sellers that use algorithmic pricing are benefitted through better visibility, sales, and timely
customer feedback. According to the retail intelligence company, Upstream Commerce, an automated
predictive and dynamic pricing tool, delivers 20% additional net profit.

content: The transportation and logistics business is undergoing massive transformations. Digital transformations,

examples of this. The key to thriving is to fine-tune strategies to stay competitive in the face of market
upheavals. Predictive analytics solutions are being used by agile firms in the sector to improve logistics
management using data-backed insights. Predictive analytics in transportation and logistics can help
suggest actions that can reduce costs and increase the chance to deliver freight on time. These
recommendations may be a change in a lane, a mode of transportation, shipping dates, or even the type of
vehicle used. This can save time and enable the organization to be nimbler to changing conditions. The
utilization of predictive analysis in transport and logistics operations management can be useful to make

transportation and vehicle fleets are outnumbered, and it is a difficult job to monitor and maintain these
vehicles despite the necessity of constant maintenance. Advanced analytics instead of preventive
maintenance enables companies to perform predictive maintenance. Predictive analytics solutions gather
vehicle data from sensors, which are then examined to identify components that are most likely to break or
underperform. This enables technicians to make necessary repair/replace decisions and avoid expensive

decisions to augment the use of the company’s equipment and transportation infrastructure.

IMPROVES DECISION-MAKING
content: Predictive analytics is a fundamental part of the manufacturing sector. Several business trends, including
globalization, vertical integration, and margin pressure, are prompting manufacturers to look for new and
novel methods to use predictive analytics to improve decision-making and performance. The
manufacturing vertical has taken a long time to embrace analytics. Applying analytics to a wide variety of
business domains, from finance and supply chain to sales and marketing and product creation, is currently
affecting other sectors. Manufacturing companies depend on a wide range of external suppliers that
provide materials, technology, data, consulting, and professional services. Since products are often at the
hub of a manufacturing company, the first phase of analytics is frequently focused on improving product
development. Common focus areas include supply chain optimization, sales and marketing budget
management, warranty cost reduction, and general financial management. Innovative insights in these
areas can have a significant influence on business performance and can provide a significant return on an
organization's analytics investment. Analytics can offer new business models based on the sale of services
rather than merely products. Predictive analytics plays an important part in manufacturing, planning,
warranty analysis, and supply chain intelligence, among others. Customers demand quality products at
lower prices with faster delivery; hence, it is vital for manufacturers to deliver a differentiated experience
throughout the entire customer life cycle. Through the implementation of predictive analytics,
manufacturers can predict the tendency of prospects to purchase and the level to which they would accept
given offers. By analyzing group behavior, manufacturers can plan logistics and operations that are based
on the demand for a particular type of product in a region.
With the advent of technologies, such as the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), predictive analytics is
becoming more intelligent and empowering the manufacturing vertical. Along with the rising demand,
manufactures are also using the capabilities of predictive analytics to enhance their production abilities.
Countries such as the US and China have used predictive analytics to improve manufacturing at a global
scale. There will be prominent use of predictive analytics solutions in the manufacturing vertical for
predictive maintenance, asset management, and remote monitoring applications. The adoption of
predictive analytics would help IT departments improve individual operations and manage a huge volume
of databases across entire organizations. As companies are becoming more versatile, IT departments are
facing challenges in the management of assets. This increases the responsibility of managing assets,
which drives the IT industry to adopt predictive analytics solutions
