content: Pressures on healthcare and life sciences companies worldwide to cut costs, enhance coordination and
outcomes, give more with less, and be more patient-centric are growing. This is driving the growth of the
predictive analytics industry. Randomized clinical trials are costly to run and ineffective in detecting rare
occurrences, treatment effects that are heterogeneous, or long-term outcomes. To find such connections,
life sciences companies use predictive analytics in healthcare. Asserting causal relationships, on the other
hand, can be challenging since data can be easily misread to make unrelated elements appear
interdependent. Predictive analytics helps in decision-making by providing real-time information that can
support decisions and deliver actionable insights for the vertical. It offers insights that can aid in enhancing
the efforts put into patient care, enhance services, and improve existing procedures. Predictive analytics
helps in providing new innovative solutions and treatments that can be properly tracked, measured, and
analyzed in the vertical. The oldest group of organizations delivering predictive analytics services in the
healthcare and life sciences industries are IBM and SAS. These companies, which were founded long
before the dot-com bubble, have formed relationships with a huge number of Fortune 500 companies.
They use these connections to provide predictive analytics services. Real-time Electronic Health Records
(EHRs) data analytics has helped a hospital located in Texas, US, cut patient readmission by 5%, indicating

sections.heading: DEMAND FOR INTELLIGENT PRODUCTION, DISTRIBUTION, AND
CONSUMPTION OF ENERGY AND UTILITIES DRIVE PREDICTIVE
ANALYTICS SOLUTIONS
content: There is a good level of adoption of predictive analytics solutions in the energy and utilities vertical. Faced
with fluctuating demand and the rising consumer interest in renewable energy, energy and utility firms are
looking at alternative energy sources to distribute new services to customers and discover new revenue
streams. Consumers now have more options than ever before, thanks to deregulation, which has forced
providers to cut costs and prices effectively. Predictive analytics is important in this vertical, which enables
intelligent production, distribution, and consumption of energy and utilities. Predictive analytics helps
monitor vast volumes of real-time data to estimate the generation and consumption patterns, predict
shortage in energy supply and future demand by studying patterns, and help optimize the energy supply
and demand cycle. Predictive analytics makes it simple for energy analysts to prepare, combine, analyze
data from various sources, and execute analytics. Factors such as changing political conditions and the
economic environment create an opportunity for vendors to deliver predictive analytics solutions to help
energy and utility service providers tackle challenges related to the internal and external environment. One
of the major drivers to plan for the future is to recognize unseen patterns and trends to anticipate
fluctuations. Predictive analytics can assist in finding both new and historical trends, which can be
combined with other correlated factors to create a plan, helping organizations to become proactive to cope
up with market demands and trends. Organizations operating in the energy and utilities vertical are
required to forecast demand and load, respectively. In the case of utilities, it is mandatory to submit an
accurate requirement to forecast load at regular intervals.
A huge chunk of data is generated from oil wells, utility grids, gas grids, smart grids, and other sensors.
This terabyte of data from both structured and unstructured sources is needed to be analyzed and get real-
time insights; hence, the vertical is in search of advanced analytical tools to get actionable insights.
Considering the transformation in the energy and utilities vertical, there is a huge possibility of facing
unprecedented challenges, such as the rising cost of operations, changing regulations, rising
environmental concerns, and meeting the changing consumer expectations. Cutting excess costs and
managing resources are some of the prominent factors driving the adoption of advanced tools in
respective verticals. The deployment of technologies such as Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) and
Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems is also helping in improving the amount and
quality of data that the utilities vertical supplies and distributes.

Rapid adoption of digitally innovative solutions and presence of
tech giants to drive market growth
According to a recent report by an industry expert, the US accounted for the highest tech market share in
the world, representing 32% of the total share, or approximately USD 1.7 trillion in 2020. The US is the
major contributor to the North American region in data generation and technological adoption. The
presence of leading global players has resulted in the early adoption of these solutions among companies
and is the major factor that has consistently kept the country a leader in every business aspect. The major
verticals contributing to the high adoption of predictive analytics include healthcare, BFSI, retail,
manufacturing, and government and defense. The US government provides support by promoting an ideal
environment for research and innovation; this has led developers to invest aggressively in new solutions
that effectively integrate the functionalities of various established tools. The Defense Advanced Research
Projects Agency (DARPA), in collaboration with commercial technology experts, developed a platform that
monitors dubious online advertisements and infers connections between them and child trafficking rings.
Moreover, data-related regulations are the other prominent factors contributing to the adoption of
predictive analytics solutions across various verticals. As communities across the country continue to relax
social distancing orders, it will be crucial for health systems to plan for changes in healthcare demands
and a surge in the number of COVID-19 patients. The team at CommonSpirit Health built predictive models
using de-identified cell phone data, public health information, and data from the system’s own care sites.
According to a research study in the US, during the COVID-19 epidemic, 50% of individuals predicted that
cloud usage would be more than expected. Vendors in the country are investing in these technologies to
provide better functioning of predictive analytics solutions to the users to make timely decisions and
increase the way of making faster business decisions for increasing business revenue.

sections.heading: Canada
content: The startup ecosystem of Canada is strong, and Canada's startups bring technologies to the market
quickly. Canadian organizations are expected to adopt the predictive analytics software aggressively during
the forecast period. Although the country is not on par with the US in the adoption of predictive analytics
solutions, various Canadian enterprises are focusing on embracing predictive analytics technology. The
country has also set up an institution, Canada.ai, which would provide information related to
advancements in AI and ML research to various startups and enterprises. With updated regulations,
businesses are now facing big penalties as a result of non-compliance with laws.
In many cases, every year, companies are adjusting their strategies for their existing database solutions
and trying to transform into data-driven organizations. Moreover, the country has mitigated financial losses
and risks, and credit card providers and other financial institutions have implemented fraud monitoring
solutions, such as Predictive Analytics Technologies (PAT), as a part of the fraud prevention programs, to
reduce credit card fraud. These factors are some of the contributors that are driving the adoption of
predictive analytics solutions in Canada. Despite the dearth of direct information on the predictive analytics
market in Canada, the country, similar to the rest of North America and the world, is on its path to
comprehensive adoption and use of predictive analytics.

sections.heading: EUROPE
content: Achievements of Europe in science and technology have been significant. R&D is an integral part of the
European economy. The robust economic infrastructure and the high internet penetration make Europe
one of the top markets for cloud-based services, which show a high contribution in the predictive analytics
market. The SMEs in the UK, Germany, and France are investing in incorporating analytical platforms to
leverage benefits, in turn, reducing unwanted costs. As the economic turmoil continues in Europe,
enterprises are likely to undertake a stronger cost containment stance sooner. The major countries
considered in the region for analysis are the UK, Germany, France, and Rest of Europe.
Along with these countries, several other European countries are also incorporating predictive analytics
solutions and services into their existing IT portfolios to deliver quick and actionable executive insights and
keep pace with competitors from other regions. The cloud industry in the UK has an established base of
business customers who understand the cloud value proposition. Enterprises in the region have strong
technical expertise, along with bigger Information Technology (IT) budgets to enable innovative predictive
analytics solutions. The European brands are adopting digital transformation through migration from legacy
systems to virtual environments at a slow pace. New technologies and business models are being
introduced rapidly in the European region due to the fast-changing business requirements. Continuous
innovations and increased spending on the adoption of newer technologies are the results of a widespread
shift in customer demands and dynamic changes in the business models of today’s data-driven industry.
The low cost of analytics components, cloud adoption, and the increasing usage of the web and higher
speed broadband connectivity across the region are some of the driving factors expected to drive the
adoption of predictive analytics in this region. Though Europe’s technology domain has been witnessing a
slower growth compared to North America, the recent investments in this region by American technology

optimize production processes, predict machinery failures, and develop more efficient smart services.

General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
GDPR (Regulation [EU] 2016/679) is a regulation by which the European Parliament, the Council of the
European Union, and the European Commission ensure the safety of the EU citizens from privacy and data
breaches. GDPR extends the scope of the EU data protection law for all foreign organizations that process
the data of EU citizens. It delivers the coordination of data protection regulations throughout the EU,
thereby making it easier for non-European companies to comply with the regulations. However, if the
regulations are not complied with, companies may have to pay four percent of their worldwide turnover as
a penalty. Key privacy and data protection requirements of GDPR include the following:

Advanced IT infrastructure, technologies, and continued
transition toward online services to drive growth in the UK
The UK is one of the strongest economies in Europe. The predictive analytics market in the UK is becoming
relentless because of the examination of high-volume information, the speed of information growth, and
the assortment of information utilized for viable business decisions. Real-time information is imperative for
verticals, such as the BFSI and healthcare, for the proficient processing of unstructured information. Apart
from this, utilizing advanced predictive analytics solutions is expected to drive market growth in the UK.
Additionally, the implementation of predictive analytics solutions by universities is expected to propel
market growth in this region. The predictive analytics market growth is expected to be driven by the
continued transition toward online services due to the relative ease and speed they can be accessed. The
increasing user access and simplicity stem from technological advances.
The savings offered by moving online, in terms of money and time, will also be a significant factor for this
transition. In addition, the need for risk management and the adoption of cloud-based technology by large,
medium, and small businesses are propelling this region forward. Following the COVID-19 lockdown in the
UK, giving customers with consistently good digital experience has been vital, regardless of the industry.
The UK and European policymakers are encouraging the governments of the countries to increase their
data capture and adopt predictive analytics for pushing the digital economy, which are the driving factors
for the predictive analytics market in the region. A resolution was passed by the European Parliament to

Government initiatives for tech nological developments in

Germany is one of the world’s leading industrial countries. It is one of the most active players in adopting
innovative digital technologies across industry verticals and is one of the leading countries for investments
around data management solutions in the European region. The German government plays an important
role in strengthening the country’s position in the manufacturing vertical. The High-Tech Strategy 2020
describes Germany’s priorities in the field of technology. To increase digitalization, the German government
would spend approximately USD 4 billion on AI products and services by 2025. Predictive analytics helps
manufacturers share new designs or product data.
In May 2021, the World Health Organization (WHO) and the German Federal Republic have announced the
creation of a new worldwide center for pandemic and epidemic intelligence, data, surveillance, and
analytics innovation. Predictive analytics has numerous applications in the manufacturing industry,
including forecasting, text mining for product development, predictive maintenance and logistics, risk
management and prevention, and stream mining and real-time prediction. Various government-funded
organizations, such as The German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI) and non-profit Open
Knowledge Foundation Germany, have partnered with corporations, such as Siemens and AGT
International, in an initiative called the Big Project.

aerospace and defense, and manufacturing verticals to drive the

sections.heading: growth in France
content: France has widespread internet penetration. According to reports, France has consistently been one of the
top R&D patent producers, and its strong hold in retail, aerospace and defense, and manufacturing
verticals has resulted in a significant rise in the predictive analytics market by companies operating in the
country. According to a survey, reshaping government services through digitalization could save the French
government USD 14.4 billion annually within five years. As part of this support plan, the government plans
to spend a significant amount of money on all things digital, including startup investment, infrastructure
investment, and digital transformation. This is expected to further drive the adoption of predictive analytics,
which would enable the government to create a better economic impact and provide users with a better
experience. France is already one of the leading countries for smart grids and smart cities, which has
contributed to the adoption of the predictive analytics market. In May 2018, Alteryx expanded its presence
by opening offices in France, which is expected to help vendors in the country to experience faster
business decisions with the use of the modern Alteryx analytics platform. Despite the French government’s
significant steps to help businesses and workers, including a record amount of stimulus, the latest
projections suggest that France's GDP would fall by 8% this year. Simultaneously, the crisis is expected to
present unique chances for consolidation and, possibly, a more efficient and resilient M&A strategy.

Predictive analytics has lately emerged as a boon for offering different levels of transformation in

forum for providing cloud services to government agencies.

sections.heading: ASIA PACIFIC

experience extensive growth opportunities in the overall predictive analytics market over the next few
years. The technology industry, including mobile, social networking, cloud, and IoT, in the region, is rapidly
developing and disrupting. Digital leaders are strategizing to optimize operations and enhance customer
experiences. Companies operating in APAC continue to focus on improving customer services to drive
market competitiveness and revenue growth. The rapid growth of the predictive analytics market in the
APAC region can be attributed to the massive growth in business deals and transactions, such as mergers
and acquisitions, joint ventures, and fundraising, across all the industry verticals in the region. The rapid

Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)
PDPA establishes a data protection law that comprises various rules governing the collection, use,
disclosure, and care of personal data in Singapore. It recognizes both the rights of individuals to protect
their personal data, including rights of access and correction, and the need of organizations to collect, use,
or disclose personal data for legitimate and reasonable purposes. The PDPA provides a national Do Not
Call (DNC) registry for establishments. The DNC Registry enables individuals to register their Singaporean
telephone numbers to opt out of receiving marketing phone calls and mobile text messages, such as Short
Message Service (SMS) or Multimedia Messaging Service (MMS), and faxes from organizations.
The PDPA covers personal data stored in electronic and non-electronic forms. The data protection
provisions in PDPA (parts III to VI) generally do not apply to the following:

sections.heading: ◼
content: Any individual acting on a personal or domestic basis

sections.heading: ◼
content: Any employee acting in the course of their employment with an organization

sections.heading: ◼
content: Any public agency or an organization in the course of acting on behalf of a public agency in
relation to the collection, use, or disclosure of the personal data; companies can refer to the
Personal Data Protection (Statutory Bodies) Notification 2013 for the list of specified public

sections.heading: ◼
content: Business contact information: This refers to an individual’s name, position name or title,
business telephone number, business address, business electronic mail address or business
fax number, and any other similar information related to the individual, not provided by the
individual solely for their personal purposes
These rules act as a baseline law operating as part of the law of Singapore. They do not supersede the
existing statutes, such as the Banking Act and Insurance Act, but work in conjunction with them and the
International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 27001
The ISO 27001 compliance provides a risk-based framework of policies and procedures for establishing,
implementing, operating, monitoring, reviewing, maintaining, and improving the Information Security
Management System (ISMS). The procedures and policies include defining a security policy and the scope
of ISMS, conducting risk assessments, managing identified risks, selecting control objectives and controls
to be implemented, and preparing a statement of applicability. ISO 27001 guidelines cover various areas,
such as access control, audit, incident response, and system and information integrity. The key 114
controls required as a part of ISO 27001 compliance are security policy; organization of information
security; asset management; HR security; physical and environmental security; communications and
operations management; access control; information systems acquisition, development, and maintenance;
information security incident management; business continuity management; and compliance.

content: Brazil Data Protection Law

sections.heading: ◼
content: Brazil’s data protection law, Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD), came into force in August
2020. Before the LGPD, the data protection legislation in Brazil was sector-based and primarily
regulated by the country’s civil rights framework for the Internet (Internet Act) and Consumer

sections.heading: ◼
content: The LGPD attempts to unify over 40 different statutes that currently govern personal data, both
online and offline, by replacing certain regulations and supplementing others.

sections.heading: ◼
content: The LGPD imposes detailed rules for the collection, use, processing, and storage of personal
data. This new regulation replaces more than 40 different regulations that deal with data
protection. The final version of the LGPD also introduced important revisions to the original
version of the law, such as the creation of the National Data Protection Authority that will be
responsible for overseeing and enforcing the LGPD.
Argentina Personal Data Protection Law No. 25.326

sections.heading: ◼
content: Argentina was the first Latin American country to implement data protection laws and the first
non-European country to be recognized by the European Commission as having adequate levels
of data protection. The need to revisit the current legislation is a result of technological
advances and the changing international landscape with the introduction of the GDPR since the
Argentinian Personal Data Protection Act 2000 came into force.

sections.heading: ◼
content: Argentina’s Personal Data Protection Law No. 25.326 has guided how data is processed and
protected. For the past year, lawmakers have debated a replacement bill that would more
closely align with GDPR. Among other mandates, it requires that employers obtain consent from
individuals before data is collected. The new bill expressly permits and regulates background
checks and provides individuals with the right to access and request the deletion of their
personal data. The replacement bill will go before the Senate, where it has a high likelihood of
passing. If the bill passes into law, organizations will have a two-year period to prepare before

sections.heading: ◼
content: Argentina’s new draft data protection bill proposes further changes to bring the country’s data
protection law in line with the GDPR. The bill acknowledges the right to be forgotten and the
right to data portability. The other changes include stricter provisions in the area of cross-border
transfers to countries with inadequate levels of data protection, new legal bases for data
processing other than data subject consent, including legitimate interests, and new definitions
of biometric and genetic data.

content: The Rest of Latin America includes Argentina, Colombia, Peru, and Chile. Various factors have limited the

government regulations, and the lack of technological awareness and a skilled IT workforce. These
countries contributed to the growth of the predictive analytics market in the region but are still behind
